items.title: The Louisiana Bowl
items.meta: A chicken nugget rice bowl with Popeye's known flavours!
items.body:
I think a Chicken Nugget Rice Bowl featuring Popeyes' signature flavours would be a great addition to the menu. It would give Popeyes a trendy new item without requiring a large investment, since it could be made using ingredients the brand already has. This would help keep costs low while introducing something fresh and exciting for customers.

Rice bowls have become increasingly popular because they are convenient, filling, and customizable. Many people choose bowls as a meal option because they offer a balanced combination of protein, rice, and toppings in one dish. By combining crispy Popeyes chicken nuggets with seasoned rice and the brand's well known sauces and flavours, Popeyes could create a menu item that appeals to both existing customers and new consumers looking for a satisfying bowl style meal.

items.title: Dove Perfume
items.meta: Dove's Iconic Soap Bar, Turned Into a Subtle Perfume!
items.body:
I think a Dove perfume would be a great way for the brand to generate new excitement and attract more customers. It could also fill a gap in the fragrance market by offering a scent designed for people who are sensitive to strong smells. Many perfumes can be overpowering, even those marketed as fresh or clean, so Dove could appeal to consumers looking for a lighter, more comfortable daily fragrance.

A Dove perfume would not only serve this audience but could also boost sales among loyal customers who already love Dove's iconic clean, soapy scent. The fragrance line could launch with two options:

Original Dove: a perfume that smells exactly like the classic Dove Beauty Bar, featuring the brand's signature clean, fresh, and comforting scent.
Pink Dove: inspired by the Pink Beauty Bar, with a more floral fragrance that is slightly stronger and more feminine while still maintaining Dove's fresh and clean identity.

By offering both scents, Dove could appeal to fans of its classic fragrance as well as those who prefer a floral variation, while staying true to the brand's reputation for gentle beauty products.

items.title: EOS Mochi Campaign
items.meta: EOS is making a comeback with new flavours!
items.body: I think EOS has a unique shape and a playful identity that could be further explored. Creating a new mochi inspired product line featuring trending flavours like matcha and mango could help elevate the brand and bring it back into the social media conversation. The mochi collection could also attract a wider range of consumers while playing into EOS’s iconic shape and recognizable design.

items.title: Fizz Mobile Reinvented
items.meta: I think Fizz has a great opportunity to differentiate itself through its marketing.
items.body:
I saw an ad from Fizz Mobile and immediately thought about how unique the name is and how much creative potential it has. The word “Fizz” naturally makes me think of something fizzy, like soda, so I wanted to play with that connection more directly. I thought it could be interesting to bring soda inspired visuals and language into the brand’s advertising, while still tying everything back to mobile plans. The goal was to create something clever, playful, and memorable, an ad that makes you stop for a second, get the reference, and think, “That’s actually pretty clever.” By using soda references, Fizz could turn its name into a bigger part of its creative identity.

 I wanted to use a soda reference by saying, “Never let your data go flat,” since people don’t like flat soda without fizz. The idea is to connect that concept to Fizz Mobile: your data never gets cut off or runs out, and Fizz keeps your mobile experience smooth while adding that extra “fizz.”

gallery.title: Original Fizz Ad
gallery.caption: This was the ad I saw and sparked my idea.

gallery.title: Crack Open A New Plan
gallery.caption: I wanted to turn the phone into a soda can to communicate the idea of “cracking open” a new phone plan. Even though switching plans can feel like a bigger investment for users, Fizz offers a positive change with affordable prices. Since it’s also a newer brand in the market, I wanted the concept to be memorable and help keep Fizz top of mind.

items.title: Degree Deodorant: My Take On This Ad
items.meta: I saw this degree ad on the NYC subway and immediately thought it could be better.
items.body:
Walking down the stairs in the NYC subway, I saw a Degree deodorant ad that read, “Unnaturally hot days call for more than natural deodorant.” I felt this wording could unintentionally suggest that Degree deodorant is less natural or less healthy because it’s positioned as something you need when natural deodorant isn’t enough.

Instead, I wanted to flip the message and focus on the confidence and freshness Degree provides, especially on hot days. Since the original ad was placed in a subway, I also thought it would be more effective to make the concept feel specific to the environment and extend it across subway systems in North America.

gallery.title: My Revision
gallery.caption: I used ChatGPT to add the text and fonts onto the subway image, but the concepts and ad copy were my own ideas.

items.title: Clutch: Car Shopping Convenience: My Take On This Ad
items.meta: I wanted to showcase how easy Clutch is for the user.
items.body: Clutch is an online platform that makes buying a used car simple and convenient. Each vehicle is certified and can be purchased entirely online, eliminating the need to visit multiple dealerships. For my take on the original ad, I wanted to emphasize this convenience and speak to consumers with busy lives who may not have the time to travel between dealerships comparing different vehicles. I created two ad concepts with different copy approaches, both highlighting how Clutch takes care of the time consuming parts of car shopping so customers can focus on what matters most to them: finding the right vehicle and getting the best value.

gallery.title: My Revised Ad #1
gallery.caption: I wanted to showcase how easily you can find and purchase a car directly from your phone, while having the confidence that Clutch has taken care of any necessary repairs and completed a safety inspection. This allows customers to have a car delivered right to their doorstep without ever having to leave home.

gallery.title: My Revised Ad #2
gallery.caption: I wanted to showcase that the only thing customers need to worry about is the car’s features, design, and what will add value to their lives. They don’t have to worry about inspecting the car in person, dealing with potential damage, or navigating the hassle of car shopping and different salespeople at a dealership. Instead, they can focus on the exciting parts of choosing a car and leave the rest to Clutch.

items.title: Blue Crayon
items.meta: Short film — written and directed by me
items.body:
Blue Crayon is a short film that I wrote and directed, inspired by my own experiences growing up with a younger brother who has severe autism and an intellectual disability.

For a university project, I wanted to tell a story that reflected a side of having an autistic sibling that is often overlooked. Popular portrayals, such as *Young Sheldon* or *The Good Doctor*, can sometimes create the impression that autism is primarily associated with exceptional intelligence or unique abilities. My experience has been much more complicated.

Growing up with my brother also meant experiencing challenging moments, including emotional outbursts, difficult behaviours, and the ways these experiences can affect family relationships. It can sometimes feel as though the needs of the neurodivergent sibling take priority, leaving other siblings feeling overlooked or pushed aside. This experience is sometimes described as being a “glass child.”

Blue Crayon is not about blaming anyone. I understand that these circumstances are often nobody’s fault, and that families are doing their best to navigate difficult situations. Instead, I wanted to create a relatable and honest story for people who may have experienced something similar, while giving others a perspective they may not have considered before.

liveEvents.title: Hosting Live Events
liveEvents.subtitle: OLG live draws, production, and on-camera hosting
liveEvents.body: During my time at OLG, I hosted live events including The Big Spin, Bigger Spin, and Plinko. I also supported live lottery draws, filmed and edited content in Adobe Premiere Pro, and prepared final videos for OLG.ca.

gallery.title: Bigger Spin Event
gallery.caption: As the draw coordinator and host, my role was to set up the lighting for the winners, ensure all machines were functioning properly and adequately prepared for the event, audit the winning amounts, and announce the results.

gallery.title: Video Editing
gallery.caption: Using Adobe Premiere Pro, after facilitating the draws, I would edit and organize the footage, then upload them to OLG.ca for audiences to view the ball drops.

gallery.title: The Draws Studio
gallery.caption: Until April 2025, Ontario was the only province still conducting physical ball draws before transitioning to a Random Number Generator (RNG) system, like other provinces. As part of my role, I would load the balls into the machines, record the draws, document the winning numbers alongside multiple auditors, and prepare press releases for Cision Newswire announcing the results.
